      <description><p>Affordability and small businesses’ economic woes feature heavily in the House race for Wisconsin’s third district</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/03/midterm-election-results-live-updates">US midterms 2026 live – latest updates</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ng-interactive/2026/nov/03/midterm-elections-full-results-senate-house-governor-races">Track live results from all 50 states</a></p></li></ul><p>After 18 years in business, Erin Klaus is closing her storefront, a handmade artisan market in downtown Eau Claire, Wisconsin, at the end of the year.</p><p>She opened Tangled Up in Hue amid a recession, during a time when downtown was “kind of a ghost town”, weathering construction and the pandemic. But the current economic crisis proved too much.       <description><p>A truce has cooled the trade conflict, but neither country has done anything to limit the outbreak of new hostilities</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a>’s trade wars have largely fallen off the headlines. But the sense that the world’s two largest economies are plowing ahead into an overt economic conflagration has taken a back seat to other, more salient fears, about Trump ending American democracy, AI killing us all and stuff like that.</p><p>The sense of calm is misleading. Under the radar, the world is marching toward an economic war of potentially epic proportions, one that, history suggests, could well spill over into the real thing.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/01/us-china-trade-war-trump-xi">Continue reading...</a></description>
